Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.taskscheduler

Class TaskSchedulerEngine

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.taskscheduler.TaskSchedulerEngine
public final class TaskSchedulerEngine extends Object
The reliable scheduling loop at the heart of the desktop task scheduler. It owns the set of ScheduledTasks loaded from a TaskStore, decides when each is due, and fires due tasks through a TaskRunner on a worker pool - never on the timing thread, so one slow or hung task cannot delay the others.

Reliability. A single daemon "tick" thread wakes every tickMillis (one second by default, which is what gives sub-minute cron expressions their resolution) and fires everything whose next-fire time has arrived. The tick body is wrapped so no exception can ever cancel the periodic task - the classic way a naive scheduleAtFixedRate scheduler silently dies. On start-up the engine reconciles tasks that came due while the desktop was not running according to each task's MisfirePolicy, and honours @reboot cron jobs by running them once.

Concurrency guard. Each task tracks how many of its own runs are in flight; when ScheduledTask.isSkipIfRunning() is set and a run is still going, the new occurrence is recorded as TaskExecutionRecord.Status.SKIPPED rather than overlapping. A next-fire time is recomputed at dispatch time (before the run), so a long-running task never causes an immediate re-fire storm when it finally completes.

Retries. A failed run is retried up to ScheduledTask.getRetryCount() times with ScheduledTask.getRetryDelayMillis() between attempts.

The engine is thread-safe: the task/next-fire/running maps are guarded by a single lock, listeners are notified outside that lock, and store I/O is done off the timing thread.
